standard_prerequisites.use: Lets a sum of two cycle classes mapping to zero be written as a locally finite sum of divisors of rational functions on integral closed subschemes of the union.

core_obligations: Get surjectivity from the statement on closed subschemes covering the scheme (proof lines 3008-3010).

Take a pair of classes mapping to zero, write the vanishing sum as a locally finite sum of principal divisors on integral closed subschemes, and split the index set according to which of the two closed subschemes each component lies in, which is possible because the components are integral (proof lines 3011-3023).
Rearrange the resulting equation to exhibit the two classes as the pushforward of a single cycle on the scheme theoretic intersection, proving exactness in the middle (proof lines 3024-3031).
proof_roadmap: Unwind the vanishing sum and split the components between the two closed subschemes (proof lines 3011-3023).
Rearrange to exhibit a cycle on the intersection (proof lines 3024-3031).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the right exactness of the Chow group sequence of two closed subschemes whose union is the whole scheme, with the first map the difference of the two pushforwards from the scheme theoretic intersection (statement lines 2990-3006, tag 0F94). Surjectivity is a citation, but exactness in the middle requires a real argument: one writes the vanishing sum as a locally finite family of principal divisors, splits that family according to which closed subscheme each integral component lies in, and rearranges the equation so that the two given classes become the two pushforwards of one cycle supported on the intersection. The splitting and rearrangement are the substance, so the claim is H2.
